# Getting started

A tinyhttp route takes a request context and returns a Web Response. Use Bun 1.2 or Node 22 with TypeScript support.

```sh
bun add tinyhttp
```

```ts
import { Router } from "tinyhttp"
import { serve } from "tinyhttp/bun"

const app = new Router()
app.get("/users/:id", req => Response.json({ id: req.params.id }))
const server = serve(app, { port: 3000 })
console.info(server.url)
```

For tests, call `await app.handle("GET", "/users/42?verbose=1")` without opening a port. A missing path returns 404; a known path with another method returns 405 and an Allow header.

See [Routing](./routing.md) for matching rules and [Adapters](./adapters.md) for Node.

# Routing

Register GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE routes with their corresponding methods. Every registration returns the router.

```ts
const app = new Router()
  .get("/users/me", () => Response.json({ id: "me" }))
  .get("/users/:id", req => Response.json({ id: req.params.id }))
  .delete("/users/:id", () => new Response(null, { status: 204 }))
```

Static segments take precedence over named parameters. Routes with equal specificity keep registration order. Parameters decode percent escapes after matching; malformed escapes return 400. A parameter cannot be empty or appear twice in a route.

A GET handler answers HEAD too, retaining status and headers but discarding the body. An explicit HEAD route may be registered through a custom adapter in a future version; the current public methods do not include head().

By default trailing slashes are ignored. Pass `{ strictSlash: true }` to distinguish them. Query values are strings, repeated keys use the last value, and plus signs decode as spaces. Empty values are tracked in [issue #11](https://github.com/maya/tinyhttp/issues/11).

# Middleware

Middleware runs in registration order, wrapping the route handler. Call `next()` once to continue, or return a Response to finish early. Calling next twice is an error.

```ts
import { Router, cors, logger, jsonBody, body } from "tinyhttp"

const app = new Router()
app.use(logger(record => console.info(record)))
app.use(cors({ origin: ["https://app.example.test"] }))
app.use(jsonBody(64 * 1024))
app.post("/items", request => Response.json(body(request), { status: 201 }))
```

Put the logger first to include middleware time. Put CORS before authentication so preflight requests can complete. Limit JSON bytes before accepting the parsed body. The body helper returns unknown unless you supply a type; validate untrusted input before using it.

Use explicit allowed origins with credentials. Browsers reject wildcard origins when credentials are enabled. The current CORS helper warns about this combination; stricter configuration validation is proposed in #33.

# Adapters

The router accepts a Web Request and returns a Web Response. Adapters translate that boundary for the server runtime.

## Bun

```ts
import { Router } from "tinyhttp"
import { serve } from "tinyhttp/bun"
const server = serve(new Router().get("/", () => new Response("ok")), { port: 3000 })
await server.stop(true)
```

The Bun helper binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. Choose port 0 in integration tests to avoid collisions.

## Node

```ts
import { Router } from "tinyhttp"
import { createNodeServer } from "tinyhttp/node"
const server = createNodeServer(new Router().get("/", () => new Response("ok")))
server.listen(3000, "127.0.0.1")
```

Node requests stream into a Web Request with duplex set to half. Responses stream back without collecting their bodies first. Keep process shutdown in the host application. Client disconnect cancellation and streaming Set-Cookie handling are tracked separately.

# Recipes

## Request timing

```ts
app.use(async (_request, next) => {
  const start = performance.now()
  const response = await next()
  const headers = new Headers(response.headers)
  headers.set("server-timing", `app;dur=${performance.now() - start}`)
  return new Response(response.body, { status: response.status, headers })
})
```

## A health check

```ts
app.get("/health", () => Response.json({ status: "ok" }))
```

## JSON input

```ts
app.use(jsonBody(16 * 1024))
app.post("/echo", request => Response.json(body(request)))
```

The examples directory contains a Bun hello server and a Node users API. Keep authorization, schema validation, and storage in your application; tinyhttp handles request routing.

# tinyhttp

A 400-line HTTP router for Bun and Node. Routes take params (`/users/:id`),
the query string parses into a plain object, and a handler returns a
`Response`.

## Use it

```ts
import { Router } from "./src/router.ts"

const app = new Router()
app.get("/users/:id", (req) => Response.json({ id: req.params.id }))

const res = await app.handle("GET", "/users/42?verbose=1")
```

## Test

```sh
bun test
```

31 tests cover routing, params, and query parsing.

## Middleware

Use `app.use(cors())`, `app.use(logger())`, and `app.use(jsonBody())` before registering handlers. Middleware runs in registration order.

## Runtimes

Bun serves Web Requests directly. The Node adapter streams request and response bodies through node:http. Both use the same router and query parser.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md)
- [Routing](docs/routing.md)

- [Adapters](docs/adapters.md)

## Contributing

Run `bun install`, `bun test`, and `bun run check`. Include a failing test with a bug report. Maya reviews release changes; Cora maintains the adapters.

# tinyhttp

Keep the Web Request and Response boundary shared across Bun and Node. Add a regression test before changing routing or parsing. Use bun test and bun run check to verify a change.

Do not log request bodies, authorization headers, or query values. Ask Maya before changing public behavior. Cora reviews adapter changes. A person reviews the diff and merges the pull request.

Write docs alongside public API changes. Keep release notes linked to the merged pull requests. Keep credentials in repository secrets, never in source or run logs.
